5.0 I have heard Sh.R.K. Ahuja, Ld. Counsel for the appellants and Sh.Anil, Ld.Chief  PP for State and have carefully perused the record.

6 . 0 A t t h e o u t s e t , l e t m e d e a l w i t h t h e a p p e l l a n t ' s p l e a t h a t d e l a y i n i n i t i a t i o n o f p r o s e c u t i o n b y t h e D e p a r t m e n t d e p r i v e d h i m o f h i s v a l u a b l e r i g h t u n d e r S e c t i o n 4 6 o f F S S A c t , t o g e t t h e s a m p l e analysed by CFL.

It may be mentioned that the period for initiation of prosecution is prescribed  in section 77 FSSA, which reads as under:
Sec.77. Time limit for prosecutions Notwithstanding anything contained in   t h i s A c t , n o c o u r t s h a l l t a k e c o g n i z a n c e o f a n o f f e n c e u n d e r t h i s A c t a f t e r t h e e x p i r y of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence:
Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for reasons to be recorded  i n w r i t i n g , a p p r o v e p r o s e c u t i o n Devyani International Ltd.& Ors. vs. Food Safety Officer   Page No. 5 of 12 within an extended period of up to three years.

6.2 Ld. Counsel for the appellants also argued that the Public Analyst's report was not supplied to them, thus, preventing them for preferring appeal.
It is seen that the appellants themselves have stated   in the appeal that they were supplied the report of the Public Analysts though  s t a t e d t o b e s u p p l i e d b e l a t e d l y .
T h u s , t h e report of the Public Analyst was supplied to the appellants.
Perusal of the record  s h o w s t h a t t h e P u b l i c A n a l y s t g a v e h i s r e p o r t o n 31.10.2012.
The said report was sent by speed post to the appellants by the Designated Officer vide letter dated 19.11.2012.

Further the report was even  supplied by Ld. ADM along with notice dated 29.08.2013.
6 .

sentences.text: Thus, nothing prevented the appellants from challenging the said report within 30 days of such receipt.

But the appellants did not exercise their right under Section 46(4) FSS Act and did not  prefer any appeal against the Food Analyst's report seeking referance to  r e f e r r a l f o o d l a b o r a t o r y ( " R F L " i n s h o r t )
notified by the Food Authority, for opinion.
6.2.2 It is not in dispute that the label on the sample packet/commodity bought by the FSO did not mention batch number.
E v e n i f t h e s a i d s a m p l e h a d b e e n s e n t t o R F L , i t w o u l d n o t h a v e made any difference in view of the admitted position that the label did not bear the batch number.

In view of the same, even if the appellants' plea that they were not given an opportunity to send the s a m p l e f o o d a r t i c l e t o R F L , i s a c c e p t e d f o r a w h i l e , i t h a s r e m a i n e d u n e x p l a i n e d a s t o h o w t h e a p p e l l a n t s ' i n t e r e s t h a s b e e n p r e j u d i c e d .
Violation of 'no batch number' would not have altered.
6 . 3 I n v i e w o f t h e a b o v e , t h e c a s e l a w r e l i e d u p o n b y t h e appellants is not relevant to the present fact situation.
All the cases dealt with the provisions of  the old Act.

In Ghisa Ram's case (Supra) Hon'ble Supreme Court noted that delay in  launching of prosecution deprives the accused of his valuable right to challenge t h e A n a l y s t ' s r e p o r t u n d e r S e c t i o n 1 3 ( 2 ) F S A c t . I n t h e i n s t a n t c a s e , a s p e r t h e a p p e l l a n t s t h e m s e l v e s , t h e s a m p l e f o o d a r t i c l e was stored for serving in the restaurant, thus the same was apparently not being necessarily  s o l d / s e r v e d i n s e a l e d c o n d i t i o n .
E v e n o t h e r w i s e , t h e a p p e l l a n t s d i d n o t c h e c k t h a t t h e l a b e l o n t h e s a m p l e f o o d a r t i c l e d i d n o t b e a r b a t c h n o .

, t h u s t h e y f a i l e d t o e x e r c i s e d u e d i l i g e n c e b e f o r e s e l l i n g t h e f o o d a r t i c l e . I n v i e w o f t h e s e f a c t s a n d c i r c u m s t a n c e s , t h e a p p e l l a n t s h a v e f a i l e d t o d e m o n s t r a t e t h a t t h e y a r e
entitled to the benefit of Section 80 (B)(2) FSS Act.

7 . 2 . 1 I n v i e w o f t h e a b o v e , t h e a p p e l l a n t s ' c o n t e n t i o n t h a t they are not liable as the sample food article was stored for serving in the restaurant and absence  of batch number on the label had no relevance for the consumer, is hardly of any  consequence.

Also, suffice it to state that the purpose of the batch number is to trace the f o o d a r t i c l e t o a p a r t i c u l a r b a t c h o f t h e f o o d a r t i c l e , i n c a s e o f a n y violation/adulteration etc.
Absence of batch number would make that impossible.
The judgments  relied upon by the appellants in this regard, dealt with Section 19(2) the Old  Act/Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Also, suffice it to state that the purpose of the batch number is to trace the f o o d a r t i c l e t o a p a r t i c u l a r b a t c h o f t h e f o o d a r t i c l e , i n c a s e o f a n y violation/adulteration etc.
Absence of batch number would make that impossible.
not mentioning of the batch number rendered the sample food article as misbranded.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The judgments  relied upon by the appellants in this regard, dealt with Section 19(2) the Old  Act/Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Misbranding is punishable under Section 52 FSS Act which provides for a penalty u p t o R s . T h r e e L a c s .
, I find no reason to interfere with the impugned order.
11.0 Appeal is dismissed, accordingly.
Devyani International Ltd.& Ors. vs. Food Safety Officer Page No. 11 of 12 12.0  TCR be returned alongwith copy of the judgment.
